I see the issue now! The expression is `'(.+?)[^\\s ]* world'`. Let me analyze this:
- `.+?` - non-greedy match of any char (except newline)
- `[^\s ]*` - zero or more chars that are NOT whitespace and NOT space (but space IS whitespace, so this is just `[^\s]*`)
- ` world` - literal

Given input `'hello       world'`:
- `.+?` tries minimum: matches `h`
- `[^\s]*` then needs to match... it can match `ello` (non-whitespace)
- Then we need ` world` but next char is a space, not `w`
- Backtrack: `.+?` matches `he`, `[^\s]*` matches `llo`, still no ` world`
- Continue backtracking...
- Eventually `.+?` matches `hello      ` (including trailing spaces!), then `[^\s]*` matches nothing (next is space), then ` world` matches.

So the issue is that `.+?` is being forced to expand to include the spaces because `[^\s]*` can't match them.

The fix should be different. Instead of changing the pattern structure, I should ensure that the fill characters after `.+?` are properly escaped and matched as spaces only.
